text: Given a user who is a member of more groups than fit on one Graph page, When graph_list_user_groups is called repeatedly chaining next_page_token, Then every group is returned exactly once and the final call reports has_more=false and next_page_token=null
Given any group a user belongs to, When graph_list_user_groups is called, Then each group entry includes groupTypes, mailEnabled, and sync_source (on-premises|cloud)

Given a tenant with more groups than fit on one Graph page, When graph_list_groups is called repeatedly chaining next_page_token, Then every group is returned exactly once and the final call reports has_more=false

Given a tenant with more users than fit on one Graph page, When graph_list_users is called repeatedly chaining next_page_token, Then every user is returned exactly once and the final call reports has_more=false
Given employee_id/user_principal_name/display_name/given_name/surname are all omitted from a graph_update_user call, When the call runs, Then the PATCH body sent to Graph contains none of those keys
Given exactly one of the five new fields is passed as explicit null, When graph_update_user runs, Then the PATCH body sends that key as null and no other new key is present

Given user_principal_name is set to an address whose domain is not a verified tenant domain, When graph_update_user runs, Then it is rejected with an invalid_argument error and no PATCH call is made to Graph
Given user_principal_name is set to an address on a verified tenant domain, When graph_update_user runs, Then the PATCH call to Graph includes userPrincipalName with the new value
Given a user with an assigned manager, When graph_remove_manager is called, Then it issues DELETE /users/{id}/manager/$ref and returns status=removed
Given a user with no manager assigned (Graph returns 404 on delete), When graph_remove_manager is called, Then it returns status=no_manager rather than an error envelope

Given graph_get_user is called with no select parameter, When the request is built, Then the $select sent to Graph includes proxyAddresses, identities, employeeId, and the onPremises* fields in addition to today's default set
Given a select parameter naming a subset of fields, When graph_get_user is called, Then the $select sent to Graph is exactly those fields plus id

Given the fake Graph client raises GraphError mid-pagination, When any of graph_list_user_groups/graph_list_groups/graph_list_users is called, Then it returns the existing error envelope instead of propagating an exception

Given graph_update_user is called with no attributes at all, including none of the five new ones, When the call runs, Then it is still rejected with the existing 'Provide at least one attribute to update' error

Given a caller's access token is scoped to tenant A, When any of the six tools in this ticket is called with a user_id/group_id belonging to tenant B, Then Microsoft Graph itself returns not-found/unauthorized for the cross-tenant reference and no tenant-B data is returned
steps: Obtain a valid Graph access token scoped to a real test tenant A (not the fake client)
Identify a real user_id/group_id that exists only in a separate tenant B
Call graph_get_user, graph_update_user, graph_remove_manager, graph_list_user_groups, graph_list_groups and graph_list_users against the tenant-B id, using the tenant-A token
expect: Every call returns a 404/401-derived error envelope (not_found or unauthorized) from Graph; no tenant-B field value appears in any response
evidence: Not executed - local blind spot. This dev sandbox has no live Microsoft Graph tenant/token; the only available test double is the fake _CapturingClient used in tests/test_tools.py, which cannot exercise real Graph's own tenant-scoping (it never enforces any isolation itself -- see the Non-functional section of docs/tickets/PRD-20393.md: isolation is entirely delegated to the caller's bearer token). Needs: a real two-tenant Entra setup (tenant A token, a tenant-B user/group id) to execute the steps above.

text: Given graph_get_user is called with no select (the default profile) and the resolved user has no manager, When the Graph response has no manager key, Then the tool returns "manager": null, not an omitted key (PRD-20393-r4.md TC1)

Given graph_get_user is called with select=["proxyAddresses","manager"] and the resolved user has no manager, When the Graph response has no manager key, Then the tool returns {id, proxyAddresses, manager: null} (PRD-20393-r4.md TC2)

Given graph_get_user requests manager and the Graph response already has a populated manager object, When the tool returns, Then the manager object is unchanged -- regression guard for the has-a-manager path (PRD-20393-r4.md TC3)

Given a user_id that resolves to a real user with no manager, When graph_remove_manager is called, Then it returns {user_id, removed: false, previous_manager: null, reason: no_manager} and specifically does NOT contain "status" or "group_id" keys -- regression-confirmation guard against the 2026-11-02 retest comment 1600390000029419, whose reported {"status": "removed"} shape matches graph_remove_group_member, not this tool (PRD-20393-r4.md TC4)

Given graph_get_user is called with no select param, When the tool builds its request, Then the default $select includes onPremisesImmutableId, onPremisesSamAccountName, createdDateTime, and lastPasswordChangeDateTime -- regression-confirmation guard, same assertion as the existing test_get_user_default_select_includes_onprem_and_audit_fields (round 2/3), named under this round in direct response to the 2026-11-02 retest comment 1600390000029419 (PRD-20393-r4.md TC5)

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_remove_manager call for a user with no manager assigned, When the tool runs, Then it returns {user_id, removed: false, previous_manager: null, reason: "no_manager"} with no error, and never a bare {"status": "removed"|"no_manager"} shape -- closes comment 1600390000046979's COV1 (requirement: comment 1600390000029562 point 1, acceptance in comment 1600390000029419)

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_remove_manager call for a user with an assigned manager, When the tool runs, Then it returns {user_id, removed: true, previous_manager: {id, display_name, user_principal_name}}, and a subsequent read of the user's manager shows none -- closes comment 1600390000046979's COV2 (requirement: comment 1600390000029562 point 2, acceptance in comment 1600390000029419)

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_remove_manager call for a user_id that does not resolve to any user, When the tool runs, Then it returns a not_found error envelope, never a no_manager result -- regression guard porting ms-graph-mcp round 3's existence-disambiguation fix (src/graph_mcp/tools/users.py:770-778 at ms-graph-mcp@master) to gdap-mcp for the first time, since this round reuses that reference behaviour verbatim (comment 1600390000029562: "Use the ms-graph-mcp behaviour that QA validated on 2026-10-16 as the reference")

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_get_user call with no select param, When the tool builds its request, Then the default $select includes onPremisesImmutableId, onPremisesSamAccountName, createdDateTime, and lastPasswordChangeDateTime alongside the rest of the default profile -- closes comment 1600390000046979's COV3 (requirement: comment 1600390000029562 point 3, acceptance in comment 1600390000029419)

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_get_user call with no select (the default profile, which always expands manager) and the resolved user has no manager, When the Graph response has no manager key, Then the tool's returned JSON contains "manager": null, not an omitted key -- same contract as ms-graph-mcp round 4 (R4-AC1/TC16), ported to gdap-mcp

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_get_user call with select=["proxyAddresses","manager"] and the resolved user has no manager, When the tool runs, Then it returns {id, proxyAddresses, manager: null} -- closes comment 1600390000046979's COV4 (requirement: comment 1600390000029562 point 4, acceptance in comment 1600390000029419)

Given a gdap-mcp ms-graph-gdap_graph_get_user call requesting manager (default call or select including "manager") and the resolved user does have a manager, When the tool returns, Then the manager object is the full expanded {id, displayName, userPrincipalName} unchanged -- regression guard that the null-injection never overwrites a real value, mirrors ms-graph-mcp round 4's TC18
